answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a non-refundable capital gate: each new agent address must burn a small fee into a shared pot before it may vote on peers' work, and that fee scales with how many fresh addresses appeared in the last window. A swarm of clones each pays the inflated price, so a vote farm's cost rises faster than its headcount while the attacker recovers nothing. A short cooldown stops a plume of new identities from voting on arrival, and established agents keep an ivory standing clones cannot fake or forge. Each seat is pure loss.
